title: Technology's share of the investment-grade bond index
sub: Tech's weight in the Bloomberg Corporate Bond Index, as a % of the index: 2024, now, and the projection (above 12%)
src: Morgan Stanley IM; Investing.com / LPL - the third bar is a projection
src_full: Morgan Stanley Investment Management; Investing.com (LPL): technology's weight in investment-grade credit rose from ~9% (2024) to ~10% of the Bloomberg Corporate Bond Index, with projections above 12%. The primary reports are not on disk; the figures are the dossier's record of them (C3, marked VERIFIED there).

proof.quote: rose from ~9% (2024) to ~10% of the Bloomberg Corporate Bond Index, with projections above 12%.
Technology used to be about nine percent of the investment-grade index - the pool that feeds your bond fund. It's ten now, and the projections run past twelve.

provenance_note: P69 T25 (R26-282, 2026-09-23). v2 of ev-ig-credit-weighting-v1 with the SAME three values and colours: it adds the UNIT the source states (% of the index - `unit: "%"`, so the bars print 9% / 10% / 12% the way every other bars object in this project prints its scale, e.g. ev-capex-ocf-94-bars-v1) and a sub that states what the bars show (the index named, the unit, the three readings). The values are written as the integers they are (9.0 -> 9): a bars page prints the value token as written, and '9.0%' is not the source's figure. The third bar is a FLOOR: the source says 'above 12%' (the script 'past twelve'); the bar stands at 12 and the sub says 'above 12%' - no number above 12 is drawn because none is on disk. The v1 sub ('The pool a bond fund buys from - reweighting toward data centres') is dropped: the bars do not show data centres.
